title: Permission census: original instruments and widened census by rite, jurisdiction and period, with regional-variants gap searches: batch 5, 2026-10-22
semantics: Continuation register to permissions-batch4-2026-10-21 (70 findings) and regional-mission-permissions-2026-10-20 (49 findings); both unchanged. Same finding shape and evidence_basis vocabulary. Each finding keeps apart the permission or approval event, the component extent and any evidenced use. A permission, translation confirmation, printing permission or use regime never by itself creates a textual state, rite, ancestry or universal adoption. 'supersedes' marks a finding that replaces an earlier one in full; partial upgrades say so in relation_to_existing_register and leave the earlier finding active.

evidence_basis_vocabulary.original-instrument: The instrument's own text read in its official publication (AAS, ASS, full decree printed in Notitiae, official vatican.va text).
evidence_basis_vocabulary.official-journal-report: A dated decree summary or register entry with protocol number in the issuing body's own journal or yearbook (Notitiae Summarium decretorum, SICO approvals list).
evidence_basis_vocabulary.official-retrospective: A later official or Church-institutional account of the event (later decree recital, Dicastery web list, commission note, official news service).
evidence_basis_vocabulary.reproduced-instrument: The instrument's text read only as reproduced (or translated) by a third party.

review_files.storage: Untracked scratch WORKLOG pinned by SHA-256; findings repeat the public source URL and locus.

independent_review.reviewer: independent batch-5 cold reviewer, distinct from the lane author and the coordinator
independent_review.scope: The reviewer fetched the cited sources into its own scratch (vatican.va ASS 13, 19, 26, 27, 31, 33, 36, 41 and AAS 1, 6, 7, 16; Notitiae 1969, 1988, 1994, 2017, 2021 and 2022 issues; the Teutonic Order PDF; archive.org page images of the 1907 Collectanea, the 1893 Glagolitic Missal, Benedict XIV's Bullarium t. IV and the 1924 Braga Missal) and re-read all 29 findings at their loci: 19 original-instrument findings (10 in the vatican.va OCR text renderings, accepted as official full-text reproductions with illegible tokens stated; 9 on page images or born-digital pages), 9 decree-summary findings and 1 official retrospective, plus the four uses, four non-admissions, the three owned route notes, the six gap dispositions, the supersession of zaire-1988, duplication against the 119 earlier findings and other inventory records, ownership, path hygiene and all 136 acquisition hashes. Corrections: the Ex pastorali munere date and sanction clause had been taken from the next constitution in the Bullarium (it is dated VIII Kal. Sept. 1754 on p. 137, with a full sanction clause); the SRC Slavonic resolutions are dated to the 13 February 1892 meeting and caveated (strict count without caveats 36 -> 35); the John VIII recital no longer claims the earliest grant for the Roman Mass; the 2022 1962-Missal licence breakdown is 20 US, 4 Canada, 4 Poland, 2 England and Wales with three mislabels; the 1994 Mallorca protocol is 857/94/L; Slovene, Novara, Udine July, 1909 index, Poland 2022 and Lyon route-note overstatements were narrowed; relations now record that seven originals re-read instruments already read elsewhere and that two active pairs overlap. Not independently re-run: the full ASS/AAS regex sweeps, the AAS 17 and 37-38 negatives, the Divine Worship 2015 and web searches, and the access refusals.

original_instrument_strict.note: Strict count = findings whose own evidence_basis is original-instrument, i.e. the instrument's text was read in its original publication or an official full-text reproduction (AAS, ASS, the issuing body's compilation, a Bullarium, Notitiae full text, or the approved book's own front matter). The vatican.va ASS/AAS volumes are the Holy See's own OCR text renderings without facsimiles; they count as official full-text reproductions, and a date or word illegible there is stated in the finding. Caveated: abridged compilation text (1615), a later official reprint (1631), a non-Roman Bullarium reprint (1754), and journal printings without subscription whose date rests on an editorial heading (1893 resolutions, 1969 letter). Seven batch-5 originals are new to the register but re-read instruments already read elsewhere in the repository (listed). The batch-4 reviewer counted 19 of the 21 batch-4 originals as permission instruments, excluding an address and a video message. Of the batch-5 originals, the two listed grant nothing (an enforcement-and-publication mandate and a negative reply); three more are predominantly restrictive but define a permitted scope (benedict-xiv-ex-pastorali-munere-1754, src-slavonic-resolutions-1893, udine-vernacular-slavic-refusal-and-limited-permission-1904-03). Under the batch-4 test (an act, not an address or message) all 19 are instruments.

register_counts.active_count_note: combined_active_findings counts findings, not distinct events: two active pairs record the same permission event (the 1615 brief; the 25 April 1969 letter) as partial upgrades without supersedes.

permissions.authority: Paul V, apostolic brief 'Romanae Sedis Antistes', issued after deliberation with the cardinals general inquisitors of the Holy Office
permissions.date: 1615-06-27 (date given in the printed note's heading)
permissions.scope: Jesuits working in China and other Catholic priests there; Chinese converts once canonically ordained; valid until the Apostolic See declares otherwise, without prejudice to bishops later constituted there
permissions.book_or_component: (1) Mass celebrated with the head covered by a special cap of the vestment colour; (2) translation of the Bible into literary (not vulgar) Chinese and use of it; (3) Chinese priests may celebrate Mass and the Divine Office, administer the sacraments and perform other functions in literary Chinese, 'iuxta ritum tamen Ecclesiae Romanae'. No translated missal is approved by the brief.
permissions.established: The operative text of the 1615 faculty is read: it permits Roman-rite Mass and Office in literary Chinese by native priests, and a covered head for celebrants. It is a faculty for a language of celebration, not the approval of any book.
permissions.limit: Printed as a footnote to a 1673 entry in the Propaganda's official Collectanea (Rome, 1907); the derogation clause is elided there as 'Non obstantibus etc.', so the text is complete in its operative part only. The Holy Office decree of 26 March 1615, the brief's original, and any approval or use of the 1670 Buglio printing are not read. The 1673 entry (next finding) shows the language part was not activated by the Congregation.
permissions.locus: Collectanea S. Congregationis de Propaganda Fide, vol. 1 (Rome: Typographia Polyglotta S.C. de Propaganda Fide, 1907), printed p. 70, n. 206, note (1); archive.org item collectaneascong0001vari, PDF p. 80
permissions.actual_use_state: Faculty only; the 1673 petition (next finding) reports Jesuit use of the covered-head concession, not of Chinese-language celebration.
permissions.inspection: Whole volume PDF and text layer acquired; PDF p. 80 page image viewed (printed p. 70, both columns and the two footnotes).
permissions.relation_to_existing_register: Strengthens the 1615 brief element of existing finding china-1615-1670-1680 (which rested on Notitiae 48 (2011), a later history). That finding is retained for the 1670 printing and the reported 1680 refusal. Both findings stay active, so the 1615 brief is recorded in two active findings.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation de Propaganda Fide, particular congregation for China (C.P. pro Sinis); approved by Clement X
permissions.scope: Vicars apostolic of China (and their priests)
permissions.book_or_component: Petition asked for (a) celebrating with covered head 'as the Jesuits do by Paul V's decree of 1615' and (b) translating Scripture, the Missal and the Breviary into Chinese so that native priests could celebrate in their own language. Reply: (a) granted 'ad formam Brevis Pauli V', with petition to the Pope; (b) 'In reliquis nihil' - no grant.
permissions.established: A dated Roman decision that extended only the head-covering faculty and gave no faculty for a Chinese Missal or Breviary translation. The printed note records Clement X's approval by litterae apostolicae 'Romanus Pontifex' of 23 December 1673 (not read).
permissions.limit: Text as printed from the Congregation's archive in its own official compilation; Clement X's 1673 letter is cited, not read. The reply is silent rather than an express prohibition; it does not revoke the 1615 brief.
permissions.locus: Collectanea S.C. de Propaganda Fide, vol. 1 (1907), printed p. 70, n. 206 and note (2); archive.org PDF p. 80
permissions.actual_use_state: Petitioners report that Jesuits in China celebrate with covered head under the 1615 faculty (see uses).
permissions.inspection: PDF p. 80 page image viewed together with the text layer; marginal date reads 31 July 1673 (the text layer misreads it as 37).

permissions.authority: Urban VIII, brief 'Ecclesia Catholica', Rome, S. Maria Maggiore, sub annulo Piscatoris; countersigned M. A. Maraldus
permissions.date: 1631-04-29 signed; 1631-11-29 posted in Rome (St Peter's, Apostolic Chancery, Campo de' Fiori) by the apostolic cursors
permissions.scope: Churches, places and provinces where Mass had hitherto been celebrated in Slavonic; secular and regular clergy
permissions.book_or_component: A Slavonic (Glagolitic) Missal composed from Dalmatian missals brought to Rome and corrected by experts to the Pius V and Clement VIII emendations, conformed to the Roman Missal. The brief approves it, abrogates the old Slavonic missals printed and manuscript, and requires the new Missal within eight months of publication in Rome unless the priest prefers Latin. It recites that a Slavonic missal had not been printed for about a century.
permissions.established: A papal instrument that both approves a Church Slavonic Roman Missal and mandates its replacement of older Slavonic books, with Latin as the only alternative.
permissions.limit: Read as reprinted, Latin with a Glagolitic version, in the front matter of the 1893 Propaganda edition of the same Missal, an official reproduction rather than the 1631 print. The 1631 book itself is not inspected. A prescription to adopt is not evidence of adoption.
permissions.locus: Missale Romanum Slavonico idiomate (Rome: Typographia Polyglotta S. Congr. de Propaganda Fide, 1893), front matter printed pp. IV-V (archive.org leaves 11-12): incipit and narrative p. IV; operative, dating and posting attestation p. V
permissions.actual_use_state: Prescription only; the brief records earlier Slavonic celebration in Dalmatian churches but no dated use of the 1631 book.
permissions.inspection: Page images of leaves 11 and 12 viewed (Latin column read; Glagolitic column not transcribed).
permissions.relation_to_existing_register: New to the permission register, not a new reading: the same brief, in the same 1893 reprint (pp. IV-V), already documents stage slavonic-roman:1631 (source slavonic-roman:1893, image-inspected 2026-10-17) and inventory candidate slavonic-roman-1631.

permissions.authority: Benedict XIV, constitution 'Ex pastorali munere' (Bullarium n. XXXVIII); subscribed D. Card. Passioneus and the Pro-Datary
permissions.date: 1754-08-25 as printed in this Bullarium's dating clause ('octavo Kalendas Septembris', pontifical year XIV); its marginal gloss reads '17. Aug. 1754'; Leo XIII (1880) also gives 25 August, the SRC Slavonic resolutions (ASS 27) 26 August
permissions.scope: All clergy, secular and regular, of the Slavo-Latin rite in the Illyrian nation
permissions.book_or_component: In the Mass and the Hours they must keep literary Slavonic in Glagolitic ('Hieronymian') characters and use only Missals, altar cards and Breviaries printed by the Congregation de Propaganda Fide; vernacular Slavonic insertions are forbidden.
permissions.established: A papal constitution confining the Slavonic privilege to the literary language and to Propaganda-printed Glagolitic books, and condemning vernacular Slavonic additions.
permissions.limit: Read in a Venetian printing of Benedict XIV's Bullarium (1758), not the Roman edition or the original; the text is complete from heading to sanction clause, dating, subscriptions and registration note. The dating clause, its marginal gloss (17 August) and the SRC's 26 August do not agree; a Roman Bullarium copy or the original should decide. Cold review: the 1 September 1754 date and the abbreviated sanction clause ('Siquis autem &c.') given earlier belong to the next constitution in the volume (n. XXXIX, pallium for the bishop of Pécs, p. 139), not to this one.
permissions.locus: Sanctissimi D.N. Benedicti Papae XIV Bullarium, tomus IV (Venice: Mainardi for Occhi, 1758), n. XXXVIII, printed pp. 136-137 (archive.org PDF pp. 148-149, leaves n147-n148); summary and incipit p. 136; recital, abuses, operative 'volumus, praecipimus atque mandamus', sanction clause, dating and subscriptions p. 137
permissions.actual_use_state: The constitution reports actual practice: some priests composing Masses with prayers in vulgar Slavonic and proposing the Last Gospel and the psalm Lavabo in the vernacular, printed in Latin letters, for reading (see uses).
permissions.inspection: Lane: page crops viewed for pp. 136, 137 and 139. Cold review: page images of pp. 136-137 (leaves n147-n148) and p. 139 (n150) re-fetched and viewed; the constitution ends on p. 137, and the p. 139 dating clause belongs to n. XXXIX.

permissions.authority: Holy See (Leo XIII; plenipotentiary Card. L. Jacobini, Secretary of State) and Prince Nicholas I of Montenegro (plenipotentiary G. Sundečić)
permissions.date: 1886-08-18 signed in Rome; in force on ratification by both parties (art. XIV)
permissions.scope: Catholics of the Principality of Montenegro, under the Archbishop of Antivari (Bar)
permissions.book_or_component: Art. XI: the prayer formula 'Domine salvum fac Principem' is to be sung in the Divine Offices in the Slavonic language (the Latin column glosses the language as 'vulgo Slavonica'; the preceding word is uncertain in the OCR rendering). No other liturgical-language provision.
permissions.established: A bilateral convention fixing one Slavonic liturgical formula for the Prince within Catholic worship in Montenegro.
permissions.limit: The convention grants no Glagolitic or Slavonic Mass and names no missal; 'divinis Officiis' is not defined as the Mass. Ratification instruments are not read. Any later Glagolitic concession for Antivari needs its own instrument (none found in ASS 19-41).
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 19 (1886-87), printed pp. 219-223 (PDF pp. 219-223), 'Publicum de re sacra Conventum a S. Sede et Amaniensi Principatu initum'; art. XI p. 222, date and signatures p. 223
permissions.actual_use_state: Provision only; no dated use.
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Mediolanen.; Card. C. Aloisi-Masella (Prefect), V. Nussi (Secretary)
permissions.scope: Ambrosian-rite chaplains of the Visconti ducal patronage serving the Roman-rite church of S. Sofia (Visitation nuns), Milan
permissions.book_or_component: May celebrate according to the Ambrosian calendar and colour, except on certain solemn days of the nuns, when they conform to the calendar and Mass of the church; applies an earlier Mediolanen. decree of 16 December 1828.
permissions.established: A dated Roman permission for priests of the Ambrosian rite to celebrate their own calendar in a Roman-rite church, with a stated exception.
permissions.limit: One church; the 1828 decree is cited, not read.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 26 (1893-94), printed p. 367 (PDF p. 367), 'Mediolanen. Dubium quoad Cappellanos ritus ambrosiani'
permissions.actual_use_state: The petition presupposes current celebration by the chaplains; no dated celebration.
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation de Propaganda Fide; signed F. Aug[ustinus], Archbishop of Larissa, Pro-Secretary
permissions.scope: The Glagolitic Roman Missal printed at the Propaganda's press
permissions.book_or_component: Missale Romanum Slavonico idiomate, 'Clementis VIII, Urbani VIII et Leonis XIII auctoritate recognitum' (title page): permission to print and publish because experts judge it a faithful version of the Roman Missal in Glagolitic characters.
permissions.established: The 1893 Glagolitic Missal's own approval leaf, read in the book: a Propaganda printing permission resting on a fidelity judgement, not a new papal promulgation.
permissions.limit: A permission to print; it does not itself define which churches may use the book (governed by the 1898 and 1906 regulations already in the register). The inventory notes a source dating the approval to 1878; the leaf reads 1893.
permissions.locus: Missale Romanum Slavonico idiomate (Rome, 1893), title page (archive.org leaf 6) and approval leaf verso of title (leaf 7)
permissions.actual_use_state: Provenance only: the scanned copy carries a Ljubljana university library stamp; no dated liturgical use.
permissions.inspection: Page images of leaves 6 and 7 viewed.
permissions.relation_to_existing_register: Permission record for the book behind inventory candidate slavonic-roman-1893; the same leaf is already evidence on stage slavonic-roman:1893-witness, and the 1896 issue reprints it (source slavonic-roman:nsk1896). No new candidate.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites (ordinary meeting of 13 February 1892)
permissions.date: 1892-02-13 (ordinary meeting, as stated in the text and as recited by the SRC letters of 5 August 1898); the ASS heading prints 'Die 13 Februarii 1893'
permissions.scope: Places where Slavonic is legitimately in liturgical use
permissions.book_or_component: (I) Liturgical Slavonic must be the old language, not modern or vernacular; (II) no Mass partly Latin and partly Slavonic, but where Slavonic prevails the Epistle and Gospel sung in Latin may also be sung in Old Slavonic; (III) priests with the Slavonic right must celebrate solemn Mass and sing the Hours in Latin when attached to a Latin church, and conversely.
permissions.established: A dated Roman ruling allowing a bilingual Epistle and Gospel and prohibiting other mixing; it cites Ex pastorali munere as of 26 August 1754.
permissions.limit: Printed without subscription in ASS; the dubia themselves are not printed. The ASS heading date (13 February 1893) conflicts with the meeting date in the text and with the SRC's own recital in 1898 ('iam edixit die 13 Februarii 1892', ASS 31 (1898-99) p. 310); the finding id keeps the lane's 1893 for stability.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 27 (1894-95), printed p. 54 (PDF p. 54), 'Resolutiones S. Rituum Congregationis circa usum linguae Slavicae'
permissions.actual_use_state: Regulates existing practice; no dated celebration.
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Leo XIII on the advice of the Sacred Congregation of Rites; Card. C. Aloisi-Masella (Pro-Prefect), D. Panici (Secretary)
permissions.scope: Churches previously in legitimate possession of Old Slavonic
permissions.book_or_component: Interprets art. 1 of the SRC letters of 5 August 1898: the privilege is not extinct where use lapsed within the last thirty years not voluntarily but through necessity, for example a lack of Old Slavonic missals or of priests able to use them.
permissions.established: A papal declaration preserving the privilege where use was interrupted by a shortage of books or priests, qualifying the continuous-use test of 1898.
permissions.limit: Names no church; the list of privileged churches is not given.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 33 (1900-01), printed p. 228 (PDF p. 228), 'Dubium quoad usum linguae slavicae in sacra liturgia'
permissions.actual_use_state: Implies interrupted use in some churches for want of missals; no named instance.
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Utinen.; Card. S. Cretoni (Prefect), D. Panici (Secretary)
permissions.scope: Parishes in the eastern part of the Archdiocese of Udine whose people speak a Slavic language (petition of Archbishop P. Zamburlini)
permissions.book_or_component: (I) Passion on Good Friday in the vernacular despite immemorial custom in two parishes: refused, for low and sung Mass, and the abuse to be removed; (II) Tantum ergo and Loreto litany in the vernacular before the exposed Sacrament: refused; (III) vernacular at Communion outside Mass: refused; (IV) baptism: sponsors' questions and answers in the vernacular allowed after the Latin; (V) the prayers prescribed after Mass: allowed in a faithful version approved by the Ordinary.
permissions.established: A dated Roman ruling on a vernacular Slavic usage in the Latin rite: the Mass component (the Passion) is refused and only the post-Mass prayers are allowed.
permissions.limit: No Slavonic (Glagolitic) privilege is involved. The decree speaks of inhabitants whose speech is akin to Slavic ('sermonem linguae slavicae affinem') and of 'lingua slavica vulgaris'; it does not name Slovene, which is a geographic inference only. The parishes are not named.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), printed pp. 568-570 (PDF pp. 568-570), 'Utinen.'
permissions.actual_use_state: Reports an immemorial custom in two parishes and vernacular use introduced about twenty years before (see uses).
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Utinen.; Card. A. Tripepi (Pro-Prefect), D. Panici (Secretary)
permissions.scope: Two parishes of the Archdiocese of Udine with an immemorial Palm Sunday custom; two others with a Communion custom
permissions.book_or_component: Petition: may the immemorial vernacular Slavic singing of the Passion after the blessing and procession of palms be tolerated, or at least be permitted before the blessing of palms or immediately after a low Mass? Reply ad I: first part negative, keep the Missal rubric (Mass follows the blessing); second part affirmative with the Ordinary's consent. The decree does not say which of the two alternatives the affirmative covers; the ASS editorial note reads it as singing after a private Mass. Vernacular 'Domine non sum dignus' at Communion outside Mass and the vernacular Loreto litany before the exposed Sacrament: refused despite immemorial custom.
permissions.established: A dated refusal of a vernacular Slavic Passion between the blessing of palms and Mass, with a permission, under the Ordinary's consent, for an alternative placing outside the Mass.
permissions.limit: Parishes not named; the editorial note's gloss is not the decree.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 36 (1903-04), printed pp. 744-745 (PDF pp. 744-745), 'Utinen.'
permissions.actual_use_state: Reports immemorial customs in two plus two parishes (see uses).
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Novarien.; Card. S. Cretoni (Prefect), D. Panici (Secretary)
permissions.scope: Curates and assistant priests serving Ambrosian-rite churches in the diocese of Novara (Cannobio named)
permissions.book_or_component: May they say Mass in the Ambrosian rite by the Milan calendar but the Office in the Roman rite by the Novara calendar? Negative: they must say both Mass and Office in the Ambrosian rite.
permissions.established: A dated Roman ruling binding the curates and assistant priests of Ambrosian-rite churches in the diocese of Novara to the Ambrosian Office as well as the Ambrosian Mass. The petition reports the same custom in the dioceses of Bergamo and Pavia; the ASS editorial note generalises, the ruling does not.
permissions.limit: Does not list the Ambrosian parishes of Novara beyond Cannobio; the editorial footnote is commentary.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 41 (1908), printed pp. 116-117 (PDF pp. 116-117), 'Novarien.'
permissions.actual_use_state: Attests Ambrosian-rite parishes in Novara diocese, including Cannobio, and a custom in Bergamo and Pavia (see uses).
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Sacred Consistorial Congregation by special mandate of Pius X; signed Carolus Perosi, Substitute
permissions.date: 1909-07 (day illegible in the text rendering: 'die m Iulii 1909')
permissions.scope: All clergy concerned in the provinces of Gorizia, Zadar and Zagreb
permissions.book_or_component: Orders the SRC decree on Slavonic in the liturgy of 18 December 1906 to be inserted in the AAS and observed 'sub gravi obedientiae vinculo'; the 1906 decree text follows in full.
permissions.established: An enforcement instrument re-promulgating the 1906 Slavonic regulation in the new official journal, including its requirement that bishops submit an index of privileged churches and its Glagolitic-book requirement; the index itself is not printed.
permissions.limit: The day of the mandate is illegible in the text layer; the 1906 decree itself is already in the register. No new concession.
permissions.locus: Acta Apostolicae Sedis 1 (1909), printed pp. 577-580 (PDF pp. 577-580), S. Congregatio Consistorialis II and the appended decree
permissions.actual_use_state: Notes that the privilege is still used contrary to the rules; no dated use.
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.
permissions.relation_to_existing_register: Republishes the decree of existing finding slavonic-glagolitic-src-decree-1906.

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Mediolanen., by special papal faculties; Card. A. Vico (Pro-Prefect), A. Verde (Secretary)
permissions.scope: All priests of the Ambrosian rite of the archdiocese of Milan (petition of Card. A. Ferrari)
permissions.book_or_component: Extends Benedict XV's three Masses of All Souls (Incruentum altaris, 10 August 1915) to the Ambrosian rite: first, the Missale Ambrosianum's Mass of the Commemoration of All Souls; second, its anniversary Mass for several dead; third, its daily Mass for several dead; all with the All Souls preface of the Ambrosian Missal, and with anniversary phrases suppressed in the second Mass's prayers.
permissions.established: A dated Roman act naming the Ambrosian Missal formularies and preface to be used for the new universal privilege, and the textual adjustment.
permissions.limit: Names formularies by title only; the Ambrosian Missal edition is not identified.
permissions.locus: Acta Apostolicae Sedis 7 (1915), printed p. 497 (PDF p. 497), 'Mediolanen. De tribus Missis legendis ... a sacerdotibus ritus Ambrosiani'
permissions.actual_use_state: Permission only; no dated celebration.
permissions.inspection: vatican.va OCR volume, a text rendering without page facsimiles: the text layer of the cited pages was read; no scan of the printed page exists in this rendering.

permissions.authority: Pius XI, bull 'Inter multiplices gravesque curas'; signed O. Card. Cagiano (Chancellor), A. Card. Vico, Maurus Riggi; registered in the Apostolic Chancery, vol. XXXI n. 6
permissions.scope: All priests of the Archdiocese of Braga celebrating Mass (petition of the archbishops and priests and of the last Braga synod)
permissions.book_or_component: The Missale Bracarense prepared under Archbishop Manuel Vieira de Matos and printed at the Vatican Polyglot Press: priests must use 'hoc uno ... Missali', recognised, arranged and approved by apostolic authority. Recites Benedict XV's earlier approval of the Braga Breviary.
permissions.established: A papal bull approving the reformed Braga Missal and making it the sole Mass book of the Braga clergy.
permissions.limit: The bull approves the edition but does not itemise its contents; the Benedict XV breviary bull is cited, with its footnote date partly cut off in the viewed image.
permissions.locus: Missale Bracarense (Rome: Typis Polyglottis Vaticanis, 1924), front matter: bull on archive.org leaves n2-n4 (n1 is an emblem leaf); incipit n2, narrative n3, operative clause, dating and signatures n4
permissions.actual_use_state: Mandate for the archdiocese; no dated celebration.
permissions.inspection: Lane: page images of leaves 3 and 4 viewed, incipit in the text layer only. Cold review: leaves n1-n5 re-fetched and viewed, including the incipit leaf n2.
permissions.relation_to_existing_register: New to the register. Recorded as act 'inter-multiplices-gravesque-curas-1924' in latin-missal-acts-v1.toml (citation from the 2026-08-01 acquisition audit).

permissions.authority: Sacred Congregation of Rites; A. Card. Vico (Prefect), Alexander Verde (Secretary)
permissions.scope: The Vatican edition of the Missale Bracarense and all future printings
permissions.book_or_component: Declares the Vatican edition typical; future printings must conform and change nothing unless the Apostolic See approves, grants or orders it; later Holy See changes to Masses that also stand in the Braga Missal apply to the Braga rite; new universal feasts are to be inserted in the Braga calendar, moved to another day if the day is taken by a higher feast.
permissions.established: A typical-edition decree for a diocesan use, with standing rules for carrying over Roman changes and feasts.
permissions.limit: Reception and later Braga printings are not checked here.
permissions.locus: Missale Bracarense (1924), front matter printed p. (X), archive.org leaf 5
permissions.actual_use_state: Norm for printings; no dated use.

permissions.authority: John VIII, letter to Svatopluk of Moravia, as quoted by Leo XIII in the encyclical 'Grande munus' (30 September 1880)

permissions.book_or_component: Permits Mass to be sung in Slavonic, the Gospel and readings to be read in good Slavonic translation, and the Hours to be sung in Slavonic.
permissions.established: An official papal recital of John VIII's grant permitting Mass, the readings and the Hours in Slavonic; the encyclical names no rite for these Masses, and it also reports Methodius's plea (880) that he had used Slavonic with the leave of Hadrian II, so the recital does not establish John VIII's letter as the first papal grant. It dates Benedict XIV's confirming letters to 25 August 1754.
permissions.limit: John VIII's letter is read only as quoted (in part) by a later encyclical; neither its original nor a critical edition is read. The encyclical's own operative content is the universal feast of Cyril and Methodius, not this permission.
permissions.locus: Acta Sanctae Sedis 13 (1880), Leo XIII, 'Grande munus', printed p. 151 (quotation); dating p. 153

remaining_gaps: Original instruments still missing: Lyon 1864 brief (Numelyo down; Google and HathiTrust refused); Divine Worship 2015 decree; Chinese indult of 1949 and the Holy Office decree of 26 March 1615; Clement X 'Romanus Pontifex' (23 Dec 1673); Cologne Prot. 2282/99/L (try the Kirchlicher Anzeiger für die Erzdiözese Köln 2002-2003); Dominican CD 98/69 (ASOP 39, 1969; not on archive.org); Chiapas recognitio of 8 November 2024; Polish 1983/1984 and 2009-2013 instruments; Ruthenian 1941 circular in its original language.

Ex pastorali munere: the Venetian Bullarium's dating clause reads VIII Kal. Sept. 1754 (25 August, pontifical year XIV) with a marginal gloss of 17 August; Leo XIII (1880) gives 25 August and the SRC Slavonic resolutions (ASS 27) 26 August. A Roman Bullarium copy or the original should decide.
The 1909 Consistorial mandate's day is illegible in the vatican.va text rendering; a page facsimile of AAS 1 (1909) p. 577 is needed.
Notitiae years still unharvested for regional entries: 1965-68, 1970, 1977-80, 1983-87, 1989-93, 1995-2002, 2004-07, 2009-15; AAS 1970-2014.

Actual-use evidence remains thin: four new reported-practice records (China 1673, Slavonic vernacular 1754, Udine 1904, Novara and Bergamo/Pavia Ambrosian parishes 1908); licences and confirmations are not celebrations.

SRC Slavonic resolutions: ASS 27 heads them 13 February 1893, but their text and the SRC letters of 5 August 1898 date them to the meeting of 13 February 1892; an SRC Decreta authentica copy should decide.
limits: A bounded expansion: 29 new findings, 19 read in the issuing instrument (original publication or official full-text reproduction), 9 from official decree summaries and 1 official retrospective, spanning c. 880 (as recited) to 2022, Latin uses (Roman, Ambrosian, Braga, Hispano-Mozarabic, Lyon, Teutonic Order), Church Slavonic Roman-rite books, mission languages (Chinese, Indian, Arabic) and vernacular Slavic usage in Udine. The vatican.va AAS/ASS volumes are OCR text renderings without page facsimiles, so findings read there rest on the text layer. Five originals carry stated caveats (an official compilation with an elided clause, an official 1893 reprint of a 1631 brief, a Venetian Bullarium reprint, and two journal printings without subscription: the 1893 SRC resolutions and the 1969 letter). Seven originals re-read instruments already read elsewhere in the repository. No stage, transition, candidate or source row is added; the regional-variants dossier is unchanged; only the three owned route rows gain a batch-5 note.
